title: Quantum Fisher Information In A Strange Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper measures quantum Fisher information in a strange metal, revealing high multipartite entanglement as the strange metal state forms.
motivation: Strange metals are poorly understood quantum states; quantifying their entanglement can reveal fundamental properties.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a strange metal sample are used to extract quantum Fisher information via a witness based on dynamical spin susceptibility.
result: Quantum Fisher information increases significantly upon entering the strange metal phase, indicating the presence of genuine multipartite entanglement.
conclusion: The strange metal state is characterized by high multipartite entanglement, which may be key to understanding its anomalous transport properties.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for quantum metrology, overcoming standard quantum limit constraints.
motivation: Quantum metrology aims to achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity, but decoherence typically restricts scaling to the standard quantum limit. The authors seek to overcome this by integrating error correction directly into the sensing protocol.
method: They propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme using a bosonic code (e.g., cat code) that continuously corrects errors during the sensing process, enabling the system to maintain coherence and achieve Heisenberg scaling in time.
result: The scheme achieves a scaling of the measurement precision proportional to T^2 (Heisenberg scaling) even in the presence of noise, outperforming conventional schemes limited to T scaling.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction provides a practical route to Heisenberg-limited metrology, with potential applications in quantum sensing and fundamental tests of physics.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond the standard two-outcome case for better detection of nonlocality and entanglement in multipartite systems, and to connect them to experimentally relevant observables like spin-nematic squeezing.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements based on spin-1 observables, and analyzes their violation in terms of dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing.
result: The inequalities provide tight bounds for classical correlations and can be violated by quantum states, enabling dimension witnessing and detection of spin-nematic squeezing.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities are a useful tool for quantum information tasks in many-body systems, bridging nonlocality and quantum metrology.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators fabricated on germanium quantum well heterostructures, a key component for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Ge quantum wells host high-mobility hole gases with strong spin-orbit coupling, promising for spin qubits, but require low-loss microwave resonators for readout and coupling.
method: The authors design and fabricate superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, characterizing their internal quality factors and resilience to magnetic fields.
result: The resonators achieve high internal quality factors (Q_i > 10^5) and maintain performance in magnetic fields up to several Tesla, suitable for spin qubit operation.
conclusion: These resonators enable high-fidelity readout and coupling of Ge hole spin qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems based on spin qubits and circuit QED.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but full control over qubit phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and algorithms. Optical control offers a pathway to faster and more coherent phase operations.
method: The authors use a combination of laser pulses and microwave fields to implement geometric phase gates on a trapped-ion qubit, leveraging the internal state and motional degrees of freedom.
result: They achieve high-fidelity phase control with low error rates, demonstrating the ability to generate arbitrary complex phases on the qubit.
conclusion: Optical control of complex phases in trapped ions is feasible and can enhance the performance of quantum gates, contributing to scalable quantum computing.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally with continuous variables, which are more practical for implementation.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states (e.g., coherent states) and homodyne detection, demonstrating the core steps of ballot casting and anonymity.
result: The experiment successfully demonstrates the feasibility of quantum anonymous voting with continuous variables, achieving anonymity and correctness for two voters.
conclusion: This proof-of-concept experiment shows that continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting is viable, paving the way for scalable multi-party quantum communication protocols.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: An integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid for quantum networking.
motivation: To enable practical quantum networks, scalable and high-quality quantum light sources that operate at standard telecommunication wavelengths are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate an integrated photonic chip that generates multiple wavelength channels aligned with the ITU grid, using nonlinear optics and on-chip filtering.
result: The source produces high-purity photon pairs with low noise and high brightness across multiple ITU channels, demonstrating compatibility with existing fiber infrastructure.
conclusion: This work provides a key component for future quantum networks, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for increased quantum communication capacity.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm achieves decoding times scaling almost linearly with code length and maintains competitive error correction performance under realistic noise.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and robust, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: A Minimal Chemo-mechanical Markov Model For Rotary Catalysis Of F<sub>1</sub>-ATPase
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: A thermodynamically consistent Markov model for the rotary catalysis of F1-ATPase, matching experimental data and resolving controversies.
motivation: F1-ATPase is a key rotary motor in cellular energy transduction, but its catalytic pathways and stochastic behavior were not fully understood.
method: Developed a minimal chemo-mechanical Markov model that incorporates thermodynamic consistency and fits experimental data.
result: The model quantitatively reproduces experimental observations and reconciles prior controversies about the catalytic cycle.
conclusion: The model provides a unified framework for understanding the stochastic dynamics of F1-ATPase, with implications for molecular motors and energy transduction.

title: Towards Practical Quantum Neural Network Diagnostics With Neural Tangent Kernels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses neural tangent kernels to analyze the training dynamics of quantum neural networks, focusing on practical diagnostics.
motivation: Quantum neural networks are hard to train and diagnose; the authors aim to provide a theoretical tool to understand their behavior.
method: They apply neural tangent kernel theory to parameterized quantum circuits, deriving analytical expressions for the kernel and studying its spectral properties.
result: The neural tangent kernel captures the training dynamics and can predict generalization performance, but the approach is limited to certain architectures and shallow circuits.
conclusion: Neural tangent kernels offer a useful diagnostic for quantum neural networks, but scalability and applicability to deeper circuits remain challenges.

conclusion: The findings could lead to next-generation medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;

result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons are produced, suggesting that such structures could indeed be responsible for ball lightning.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons are a plausible explanation for ball lightning, warranting further investigation.

title: A Super-inert Near-infrared Fluorescent Rotaxane Dye For Surgical Navigation
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: A near-infrared fluorescent rotaxane dye with high photostability and renal clearance is developed for surgical navigation imaging.
motivation: To improve intraoperative imaging of ureters and other tissues using near-infrared fluorescence with better photostability and biocompatibility.
method: Synthesis of a threaded α-cyclodextrin rotaxane NIR dye and characterization of its photophysical properties, followed by in vivo imaging in mice and pigs.
result: The dye exhibits superior photostability, high solubility, negligible non-specific binding, and complete renal clearance, enabling clear ureter imaging via NIR-II and clinical NIR-I laparoscopes.
conclusion: The rotaxane dye is a promising contrast agent for surgical navigation, particularly for ureter identification.

result: They demonstrate a perovskite/perovskite/silicon tandem solar cell with a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.53%.
conclusion: The hybrid deposition approach enables efficient ultrawide-bandgap perovskites, advancing triple-junction solar cell technology.

abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 18 May 2026;

method: The authors unify results from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models using a dynamical systems viewpoint.

title: Drivers Of Technology Diffusion Speed In Countries
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the speed of technology diffusion across countries using a large dataset of 130 technologies, finding that newer, smaller, less materially intensive, and shorter-lived technologies are adopted more quickly.
motivation: Understanding the factors that influence how quickly technologies spread across countries is important for policy and innovation management.
method: The authors analyze 5,990 time series of technology adoption across 130 technologies using statistical models to identify drivers of diffusion speed.
result: Newer technologies, as well as those that are smaller, less materially intensive, and shorter-lived, tend to be adopted more quickly.
conclusion: Technology characteristics significantly affect diffusion speed, which has implications for accelerating the adoption of beneficial technologies.

title: Rossby Wave-modulated Orbital Precipitation Anomalies In The Asia-Pacific Region
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies orbital-driven convection in the Indo-Pacific Warm Pool generating Rossby waves that modulate precipitation patterns in the Asia-Pacific region.
motivation: To understand how orbital forcing influences precipitation anomalies via atmospheric dynamics.
method: Analysis of climate model simulations and observational data to link orbital convection to Rossby wave propagation.
result: Orbital-driven convection in the warm pool excites planetary Rossby waves that organize banded precipitation anomalies across the Asia-Pacific.
conclusion: Orbital-scale climate variability can be mediated by Rossby wave dynamics, impacting regional precipitation patterns.

title: Genetic And Pharmacological Inactivation Of Peptidoglycan Remodeling Increases Antibiotic Susceptibility Of Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus Faecium
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies peptidoglycan remodeling in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium to increase antibiotic susceptibility.
motivation: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium is a major clinical threat; new strategies to restore antibiotic efficacy are needed.
method: Genetic and pharmacological inactivation of peptidoglycan hydrolase SagA was performed, and antibiotic susceptibility was measured across clinical strains.
result: Inhibition of SagA restored vancomycin efficacy against multidrug-resistant clinical strains.
conclusion: Targeting peptidoglycan remodeling is a promising approach to combat antibiotic resistance in VRE.

title: Pvc Microplastics Facilitate Uropathogenic Escherichia Coli Pathogenicity By Enhancing Host Cell Invasion And Mitochondrial-dependent Pyroptosis
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how PVC microplastics enhance the pathogenicity of uropathogenic E. coli by promoting host cell invasion and mitochondrial-dependent pyroptosis.
motivation: Microplastics are environmental pollutants that may influence bacterial infections, but their role in clinical settings is poorly understood.
method: The authors exposed uropathogenic E. coli to PVC microplastics and assessed bacterial invasion, immune evasion, and host cell death pathways using in vitro and in vivo models.
result: PVC microplastics increased bacterial invasion of host cells and triggered mitochondrial-dependent pyroptosis, helping bacteria evade immune cells and increase shedding.
conclusion: PVC microplastics can facilitate acute urinary tract infections by enhancing E. coli pathogenicity, highlighting a potential health risk from microplastic pollution.

title: Carbocycle Editing Of Ketones Proceeds Via A Radical-mediated Bidirectional C-c Bond Cleavage/coupling Strategy
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a radical-mediated strategy for editing carbocycles in ketones to produce functionalized linchpins.
motivation: Current synthetic routes to alkyl linchpins suffer from poor step economy and limited functional group tolerance, motivating the development of a more efficient method.
method: The authors use gem-diperoxide intermediates to enable a bidirectional C–C bond cleavage/coupling strategy under radical conditions.
result: The method transforms cyclic ketones into diverse functionalized linchpins with improved step economy and functional group tolerance.
conclusion: This radical-mediated approach offers a new, efficient pathway for carbocycle editing and linchpin synthesis.

title: Deep Learning Completes Us Flood Hazard Maps Revealing Millions Exposed To Previously Unrecognized Risk
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to complete flood hazard maps in the US, revealing millions more people at risk.
motivation: Many areas in the US lack official flood risk data, leading to underestimation of exposure.
method: An AI model learns from existing flood hazard maps to predict flood risk for unmapped regions.
result: The model reveals over 11 million additional people exposed to flood risks, a 69% increase from official records.
conclusion: AI can significantly improve flood risk assessment and inform policy for disaster preparedness.
